summary: Arthur Woollgar Verrall studied at Wellington College (~1865–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873). He later taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Arti Dhand is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Calgary (~1989–1993) and McGill University (~1993–2000). Around 2003, she served as Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto.
Aruna Haldar worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Girindrasekhar Bose and Kedarnath Ojha, and held a teaching post at Patna University.

Indologist Arunoday Natvarlal Jani earned his Ph.D. under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt at the University of Mumbai (~1946–1953) and studied under M. V. Upadhyay. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1967–1981).

Arvind Sharma, working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard (Ph.D.). He held posts at Queensland (1976), Sydney (1980), Harvard, and held the Birks Chair in Comparative Religion at McGill (1994).

Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Professor, Department Head, and Emeritus Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Kelaniya, and became a Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. at Komazawa University (attested 1973) and served as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).

Asen Balikci, who worked in Tibetology and other fields, earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University (1956). His career included posts at the Musée d'ethnographie de Neuchâtel, the Canadian Museum of History, the National Museum of Canada, and the University of Montreal.

Ashok Kumar Chatterjee studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. He served as professor and head of the philosophy department at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and at Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the East-West Center and founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.

Ashok Narhar Aklujkar studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Specializing in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, he taught in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University. He held posts at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1967–1989).

Ashutosh Mukherjee studied at South Suburban School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. Active in Indology, history, and archaeology, he served on the Calcutta High Court, was President of the University of Calcutta and The Asiatic Society, and founded Asutosh College.

Asim Kumar Chatterjee, an Indologist and historian, earned his Ph.D. under D. Mukherjee at the University of Calcutta (~1963–1967). He served as a Senior Research Fellow at the University of Calcutta and as a lecturer in English at Jangipur College.

Indologist and linguist Asko Parpola studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies and the Academy of Finland, and served as Professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Astley John Hilary Goodwin was an archaeologist who studied at St. John's College, Johannesburg, Selwyn College, and SOAS University of London. He took up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.
Athanaric Huard, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Georges-Jean Pinault and is attested in 2026 as an Assistent at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Atsuhiko Yoshida studied at Seikei, Tokyo, Athénée Français, Strasbourg, and EPHE under Georges Dumézil. Specializing in religious studies and history/archaeology, he worked at CNRS, lectured at Geneva and UCLA, and held professorships at Seikei (1970) and Gakushuin (2006).

Atsuki Nakagami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held posts as a visiting researcher at the University of Hamburg (attested 2022) and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Atsushi Ibuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1989) and became a professor at Toyo University (~2007).
